content:
The image shows a corn ear in close-up. The kernels are yellow/orange, and between them there is visible dark green/teal-colored mold growth filling the spaces between kernels. This is a classic fungal ear rot presentation on corn.

Key observations:
- Affected part: corn ear (kernels)
- Dark green to blue-green fuzzy/powdery mold growing between and around kernels
- Kernels themselves appear intact but surrounded by the mold
- The color (dark green/teal) is characteristic of *Trichoderma* species, which produce distinctive green spores
- Not pink/red (ruling out Gibberella), not white/gray (ruling out Diplodia), not olive-brown (ruling out Aspergillus)

The dark green mold coloration is the hallmark of Trichoderma ear rot, caused by *Trichoderma* spp., which are characterized by their bright green to dark green conidia.
